imperative: Ordinary loṭ retains the śyan stem sy-. The second singular has hi-luk under 6.4.105; first persons retain the appropriate āṭ/mip changes. In this root there is no whole-root ja substitution.
blessing: 3.3.173 selects the desired but unattained event. 3.4.116/104 supply the ārdhadhātuka/kit blessing-liṅ context, and 6.4.67 supplies root e: seyāt. The sārvadhātuka present-system stem is not carried into that liṅ.
tatan_guard: 7.1.35 is an optional replacement of tu/hi only in āśis. Ordinary vidhi alone does not license syatāt. All four retained tatāṅ readings in the two profiles are guarded individually in STATE.json.
negative_controls: Do not offer praṇiṣyatāt as an unconditional ordinary command.
Do not replace ordinary praṇiṣyet by blessing praṇiṣeyāt merely because the translation uses may.
Do not take blessing loṭ as ārdhadhātuka merely because blessing liṅ is.
domain: The four inherited, sense-qualified ordered pra+ni / pari+ni P profiles. Unaccented Classical pause forms; no A-pada or yaṅ-luk expansion.
observed_and_composed: Kāśikā 6.4.66 explicitly identifies ṣo antakarmaṇi and 6.4.67 gives avaseyāt. The ordered-prefix and dental/retroflex histories are inherited through PG274/PG279. Eighteen bare archived cells are finite comparisons; the prefixed words are written compositions. The archive mixes the tatāṅ words into its imperative cells, but the written relation adds their source-required blessing guard. Zero new nominal positions and zero separately counted source observations.
